awards.title: AMA Research Challenge 2026 Top 65: Diarrhoea Screening at the Doorstep
awards.excerpt: A field study of WHO-defined diarrhoea screening during India's Pulse Polio campaign was selected in the top 65 of 1,300 posters at the AMA Research Challenge.
awards.author: USMLE Wise Team
awards.body:
This poster tests whether two WHO-defined diarrhoea questions can be added to India's Pulse Polio doorstep screening without slowing the campaign down. Volunteers screened 3,086 children aged five and under across a three-day campaign in June 2026, collecting answers on a mobile application.

  • Poster: Diarrhoea at the Doorstep: Feasibility of WHO-Defined Screening During Mass OPV Vaccination
  • Presenter: Shelja Sharma
  • Recognition: Selected in the top 65 of 1,300 posters
  • Session: AMA Research Challenge 2026 virtual poster symposium, October 13–15, 2026
  • Findings: Every caregiver answered both screening questions. 1.2% of children (38) had diarrhoea in the previous seven days and 0.3% (10) had diarrhoea on the day of screening, with no significant difference by age (p = 0.78) or location (p = 0.97).

awards.title: ACG Presidential Award: Early Microbiota Restoration for C. difficile Infection
awards.excerpt: A systematic review and meta-analysis on early gut microbiota restoration for C. diff infection won a Presidential Award at ACG's 2026 Annual Scientific Meeting.
awards.author: USMLE Wise Team
awards.body:
This poster presents a systematic review and meta-analysis examining whether restoring the gut microbiota early (at the first episode or first recurrence of C. difficile infection) improves outcomes compared with standard approaches. It pools data from randomized and comparative studies.

  • Poster: P5850 (Early Microbiota Restoration for Primary and First-Recurrent Clostridioides difficile Infection: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized and Comparative Studies)
  • Presenter: Jose Enrique Paredes Romero, MD, IESS Hospital del Norte Los Ceibos
  • Award: ACG Presidential Award Winner
  • Session: Tuesday Poster Session, Infections and Microbiome category, October 13, 2026, Exhibit Halls A–D, Level 3

awards.title: 7ANOS 2026 Second Prize: Place of Death Among US Brain Tumour Decedents
awards.excerpt: A CDC WONDER joinpoint analysis of where US brain tumour patients die took second prize in the postgraduate moderated poster category at the 7th Annual Neuro-Oncology Symposium.
awards.author: USMLE Wise Team
awards.body:
This poster tracks where people with malignant brain tumours died in the United States between 2003 and 2024, using CDC WONDER death-certificate data and joinpoint regression, then reads the trend as a template for palliative-care surveillance in Pakistan.

  • Poster: Place of Death Among Malignant Brain Tumour Decedents in the United States, 2003–2024: A CDC WONDER Joinpoint Analysis of End-of-Life Care Settings with Relevance to Palliative Capacity in Pakistan
  • Presenter: Haniah Noor Baqi, Faculty of Medicine, Caucasus International University, Tbilisi, Georgia
  • Award: Second Prize, Postgraduate Category, Moderated Poster Presentation
  • Session: 7th Annual Neuro-Oncology Symposium (7ANOS), "Neuro-Oncology in the Real World", October 2–4, 2026, Jinnah Postgraduate Medical Centre, Karachi
  • Findings: Across 335,318 decedents, home deaths rose from 45.1% in 2003 to 53.3% in 2024 and hospice deaths from 0.7% to 13.3%, while hospital inpatient deaths fell from 22.5% to 13.0% and nursing home deaths from 21.4% to 14.2%.
  • Abstract: doi:10.47391/JPMA-7ANOS-ABS-14

awards.title: ACP Illinois 2026 Second Place: Heparin Resistance in Cardiac Surgery
awards.excerpt: A systematic review and proportion meta-analysis of heparin resistance during cardiopulmonary bypass took second place in the poster competition at the ACP Illinois Chapter meeting.
awards.author: USMLE Wise Team
awards.body:
This poster pools 41 studies covering 22,403 adult cardiopulmonary bypass patients to estimate how often heparin resistance actually occurs, and shows that the headline rate depends almost entirely on which definition a centre uses.

  • Poster: Prevalence of Heparin Resistance in Adult Cardiac Surgery with Cardiopulmonary Bypass: A Systematic Review and Proportion Meta-Analysis
  • Presenter: Meghana Reddy, first author
  • Award: Second Place, Poster Presentation Category
  • Session: ACP Illinois Chapter 2026 Internal Medicine Meeting, October 2, 2026, Peoria, IL
  • Findings: Pooled prevalence of heparin resistance was 18.9% (95% CI 14.0–25.0) with extreme heterogeneity (I² = 96.9%). Estimates ran from 39.7% under heparin sensitivity and dose-response definitions to 16.1% for ACT thresholds and 5.6% for pragmatic definitions (p < 0.0001), so roughly 1 in 5 patients meets some definition of heparin resistance.

awards.title: AACP 2026 Best Poster Award: LGBTQIA+ Mental Health in Delhi
awards.excerpt: A cross-sectional study of depression, suicidal ideation, and perceived discrimination among LGBTQIA+ adults in Delhi won the Best Poster Presentation Award at AACP 2026.
awards.author: USMLE Wise Team
awards.body:
This poster reports a community-based, cross-sectional study of 92 self-identified LGBTQIA+ adults in Delhi, measuring depressive symptoms (PHQ-9), perceived minority stigma, and suicidal ideation (SIDAS), then testing how closely the three travel together.

  • Poster: Depression, Suicidal Ideation, and Perceived Discrimination in the Lesbian, Gay, Bisexual, and Transgender Population in Delhi: A Cross-sectional Study
  • Presenter: Nafiz Rashid, Dalian Medical University
  • Award: Best Poster Presentation Award
  • Session: AACP 2026, October 12, 2026
  • Findings: 75% of participants screened positive for at least mild depressive symptoms and 38% were at high risk of suicidal ideation. Participants with elevated minority stigma had 11.45 times the odds of depressive symptoms (95% CI 3.55–36.93, p < .001).
